newsitem.title: TURKEY: Death toll in Turk boat sinking rises to 16.
newsitem.headline: Death toll in Turk boat sinking rises to 16.

text.p: Turkish navy and coastguard ships searched on Friday for any survivors from a boat that sunk in the Aegean Sea earlier this week, killing at least 16 Iraqi illegal immigrants being smuggled to Greece.

"One more body was found following the three other corpses this morning," a coastguard official in the western port city of Izmir told Reuters. Eighteen people, including women and children, were still missing, he said.
The 10-metre (30-feet) boat capsized and sunk on Wednesday night after leaving for the nearby Greek island of Chios from a peninsula of the Turkish shore near the resort town of Cesme.
It was carrying an illegal cargo of 40 Iraqis who had paid more than $1,000 each for the short passage.
Iraqis, mainly Kurds, often flee economic hardships and factional strife in northern Iraq for Europe via Turkey. Flimsy boats carry them to Greek islands.
Six people were rescued and taken to local hospitals on Thursday. Two men, one Turkish, the other Iraqi, have been arrested in connection with case.
Anatolian news agency quoted one survivor as saying they were left alone on the boat without any captain or crew.
"A man, we learnt he was the captain, told us how to use the boat and the direction towards Chios and then left us alone on the boat," Osman Ali Ahmed said.
"The crying of the children and the screaming of the women are still in my ears. Nobody could help anyone...They left us to die."
The coastguard offical said intensive searches would continue until Saturday evening, but added there was little hope of finding those missing.
